register.label: Bookings included in Voi Pass
register.scope: The upgrade incentive scales with the share of bookings the Pass covers; every included booking still costs a placement. Pass holders respond to the average fee they pay per booking (nothing within the allowance). The Pass price is a calibration input, so the allowance is not a priced tier. Under the linear response, a booking that costs a Pass holder nothing doubles their reference adoption (fee 0 is a 100% cut from the 25 kr anchor), so allowances beyond about 2 a month lie outside the response’s local range.

register.label: Booking fee (incl. VAT)
register.scope: Set at 35 kr: at 25 kr a booking costs more to place and hold than it earns. The adoption inputs describe demand at the 25 kr reference fee; at 35 kr the default price response (elasticity 1) lowers adoption by 40%. The price table under Stress Test shows other responses. Benchmarks: Voi’s free-unlock add-on 29 kr a month; Dott and Lime offer 10–15 minute holds free (non-Oslo analogues: the Oslo permits are held by Voi, Ryde and Bolt).

register.label: Demand response to the fee

register.label: Use bounded logit price response
register.scope: Alternative unestimated demand structure. Linear and logit share adoption at the reference fee and the same local price elasticity there. Logit(p) = logit(p0) − elasticity × (fee − reference) / reference / (1 − p0), for 0 < p0 < 1. Price-response envelopes and the assumption challenge test both forms. Train (2009), chapter 3, motivates the probability form, not its Voi parameter values.

assumptions.label: Concentrated hub operations
assumptions.argument: Limit the first offer to approved hubs and departure windows where existing overnight supply can fulfil most bookings. Twenty percent additional placement is a design objective to test, not a measured capability.
assumptions.tradeoff: A narrower footprint may reduce customer access and adoption. Do not assume a cost improvement without checking the corresponding demand and reliability.
assumptions.measure: Extra dedicated placements per booking attempt, paired with eligible demand, walking access and on-time fulfilment.

assumptions.label: A reliable promise
assumptions.argument: A 95% fulfilment target makes the proposed assurance specific. It is an assumed service standard, not a current Voi performance observation.
assumptions.tradeoff: Higher reliability may require more vehicles, labour or restricted booking capacity.
assumptions.measure: Correct vehicle, adequate battery and promised location/time for every assigned booking attempt.

assumptions.label: Payment and repeated use
assumptions.argument: The NOK 35 fee is a test price for planned, time-sensitive departures. The model applies price response; the survey does not establish booking willingness to pay.
assumptions.tradeoff: Eight monthly bookings imply up to NOK 280 in booking fees, so frequent adoption and price must be tested jointly.
assumptions.measure: Conversion, bookings per adopter, repeat paid use and incremental contribution against assigned controls.

assumptions.label: Oslo expansion scale
assumptions.argument: The approximately 125,000 starting active customers are a constructed market estimate from dated trip inputs and assumed frequency, not an observed customer count.
assumptions.tradeoff: The 72-person convenience sample does not establish Oslo segment shares, eligible reach or adoption.
assumptions.measure: Validate the operating customer base and eligible hub-zone population before scaling; retain cohort and revenue-benchmark stresses.

assumptions.label: Resources and funding
assumptions.argument: The report conservatively treats all assigned internal work as requiring additional paid capacity. Economic resource costs remain included even if existing staff can be reassigned.
assumptions.tradeoff: Existing salary and opportunity cost are not automatically additional cash expenditure.
assumptions.measure: Finance confirms hiring, contracted work, replacement capacity and timing separately from internal resource hours.
